request: Which categories got dearer for me from the first half of 2025 to the second? Show both halves per category.

plan.title: First half against second half
plan.question: Spending of the first half of 2025 and of the second half per category, one row per category and period and never two rows for the same pair, the period named 'First half' or 'Second half', the six largest categories by total over both halves, uncategorized bookings as 'Needs review', columns topic, period and total_eur, the euro figure last.

sql:
WITH spending AS (
  SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic,
         CASE WHEN CAST(strftime('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) <= 6 THEN 'First half' ELSE 'Second half' END AS period,
         -amount AS eur
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0
), biggest AS (
  SELECT topic FROM spending GROUP BY topic ORDER BY SUM(eur) DESC LIMIT 6
)
SELECT topic, period, ROUND(SUM(eur), 2) AS total_eur
FROM spending
WHERE topic IN (SELECT topic FROM biggest)
GROUP BY topic, period
ORDER BY topic, period
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
two periods compared by category are two dimensions that cross
grouped bars put the two halves side by side for every category
the category is the position and the half is the series, so the rows come long
the period is the whole of 2025, cut in two halves
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar_grouped, so barY carries a series and layout: group()
the columns are topic, period and total_eur, and total_eur holds the numbers
period is the series, so it is the z and the color channel and the legend goes on
category names sit on x on a band scale, tilted and none dropped, euros on y from the bare factory

plan.question: Spending of 2025 per category and per account, both accounts of the profile, one row per category and account and never two rows for the same pair, uncategorized bookings as 'Needs review', columns topic, account and total_eur, the euro figure last.

sql:
SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, account, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0
GROUP BY topic, account
ORDER BY topic, account

request: Wie teilen sich unsere Ausgaben pro Quartal auf Lebensmittel, Shopping, Transport und Essengehen auf?

plan.title: Vier Kategorien je Quartal
plan.question: Ausgaben der Kategorien Groceries, Shopping, Transport und Dining je Quartal 2025, eine Zeile je Quartal und Kategorie und nie zwei Zeilen fuer dasselbe Paar, Spalten quarter als '2025-Q1', topic und total_eur, der Eurobetrag zuletzt.

sql:
SELECT '2025-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3) AS quarter,
       category AS topic,
       ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0 AND category IN ('Groceries', 'Shopping', 'Transport', 'Dining')
GROUP BY quarter, topic
ORDER BY quarter, topic
reasoning_plan:
die Anfrage ist deutsch, also ist die Sprache de
vier Kategorien ueber vier Quartale, also zwei Dimensionen, die sich kreuzen
aufteilen heisst, die Quartalssumme zaehlt mit, also gestapelte Balken
die Anfrage sagt Quartale, also traegt die Achse Quartale und keine Monate
die Spalten sind quarter, topic und total_eur, der Betrag zuletzt
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar_stacked, so barY carries a series and no layout
the columns are quarter, topic and total_eur, and total_eur holds the numbers
topic is the series, so it is the z and the color channel and the legend goes on
a quarter reads 2025-Q1, which is a name and not a month, so no monthShort and no label dropped

request: Draw the month on month change in our spending through 2025.

plan.title: Change to the month before
plan.question: For each month of 2025 from February onwards the difference between what was spent in it and what was spent the month before, signed so that a cheaper month is negative, one row per month, columns month as 'YYYY-MM' and change_eur.

sql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, SUM(-amount) AS eur
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0
  GROUP BY month
), diffs AS (
  SELECT month, eur - LAG(eur) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS change
  FROM monthly
)
SELECT month, ROUND(change, 2) AS change_eur
FROM diffs
WHERE change IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY month
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
one figure per month and no second dimension, so one bar per month
a change is a difference, so the figure is signed and a cheaper month is negative
bars rest on zero, so the cheaper months are drawn below the baseline
the period is 2025 from February onwards, because January has no month before it
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar, so the mark is barY over the rows
the columns are month and change_eur, and change_eur holds the numbers, signed
months on x on a band scale with monthShort
a bar rests on zero by itself, so its euro axis is the bare scaleLinear factory

request: Bei welchen Laeden haben wir 2025 am meisten ausgegeben?

plan.title: Groesste Laeden 2025
plan.question: Die acht Haendler mit den hoechsten Ausgaben 2025 ueber beide Konten, nach ihrem angereicherten Namen benannt, nach dem Betrag geordnet, eine Zeile je Haendler, Spalten merchant und total_eur.

sql:
SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0
GROUP BY merchant
ORDER BY total_eur DESC
LIMIT 8

barX draws sideways, so the euro column is x and the names are y

request: Show how our spending accumulated across 2025.

plan.title: Spending added up over the year
plan.question: Spending of 2025 over both accounts added up from January onwards, the running total after each month, one row per month, columns month as 'YYYY-MM' and cumulative_eur.

sql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, SUM(-amount) AS eur
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT month, ROUND(SUM(eur) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
"accumulated" is a running total, and a running total is an area
one band over twelve ordered months, so no series and no legend
the columns are the month and the running euro figure, the figure last
the period is the whole of 2025, both accounts together
reasoning_code:
the shape is area, so areaY draws the band and lineY its edge
the columns are month and cumulative_eur, and cumulative_eur holds the numbers
months on x with monthShort, euros on y
an area rests on zero, so its euro axis is the bare scaleLinear factory
